text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. Each time this happens, automated builds start immediately, so the team does not need to build the software by hand. As part of the same process, the system runs tests to check that everything works correctly. This helps catch issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines usually include several steps, such as building, testing, and reporting results. By following this approach, teams can find mistakes quickly, save time, and release better software.
